summary:
FireTrace helps land and forest managers examine historical burning patterns without mistaking a change of satellite sensor for a change on the ground. We built a web application that brings MODIS and VIIRS observations into a transparent burning activity calendar, with an inspectable sensor comparison and a portable evidence record.

Our demonstration uses 16,258 actual NASA FIRMS records from a declared study rectangle in Vietnam's Central Highlands, spanning 2001–2024. Users can explore recorded seasonal patterns, change assumptions while retaining the source, and export their review with its underlying evidence. We fit the comparison on 2013–2020 data and report separate 2021–2024 results, including poor FRP agreement.

FireTrace keeps missing coverage explicit and reports UNVERIFIABLE when the evidence cannot support a verified hazard conclusion. It gives managers a reproducible starting point for local review; independent incident validation and testing with land managers are the next steps.
details:
The problem and the people we serve

A forest or land manager comparing hotspot totals across years can mistake a sensor transition for a change on the ground. MODIS and VIIRS observe thermal activity with different footprints and sampling. A larger detection count alone cannot establish more physical fires, a greater burned area, or future danger.

FireTrace addresses the challenge's burning activity calendar through a practical review task: choose a study area, inspect recorded seasonal periods, and retain the evidence before consulting local incident and land-cover records. Land managers are our primary users; the same transparent comparisons can support scientific review and discussion with emergency-response teams.

NASA data is the foundation

The working case uses 37 NASA FIRMS country-archive files. A reproducible clip retains 16,258 original observations inside a Central Highlands rectangle in Vietnam: 4,143 MODIS rows from 2001–2024 and 12,115 Suomi NPP VIIRS rows from 2012–2024. These are original row counts before analysis filters.

The manifest records the original URLs, retrieval metadata, versions, byte sizes and SHA-256 hashes. Our builder preserves NASA measurement fields rather than generating replacement values. The extent is an analysis rectangle, not an established administrative, forest, or protected-area boundary. Separately labeled generated presets and synthetic CSVs demonstrate software behavior; they are not evidence of real regional conditions.

How the application works

An original Python pipeline normalizes sensor fields, confidence, and time, then groups observations into 1 km sinusoidal cell windows. A fitted multiplier relates sensor-family occupancy. HHE, our resulting measure, is a weighted occupancy index rather than a physical fire count. A separate fit scales matched VIIRS fire radiative power (FRP), which remains sampled power in megawatts, not energy.

For the NASA case, both fits use 2013–2020 observations and remain fixed during the separate 2021–2024 assessment. The available 2001–2020 same-month reference is descriptive. Changing the displayed period or audience retains the source and model. Confidence and source-type filters use their declared training profile. Missing observations remain unknown rather than becoming zero activity.

What our evidence shows

With nominal-or-higher confidence and the supplied non-vegetation guard enabled, held-out occupancy agreement has 43 positive monthly pairs, R² 0.841 and RMSE 3.93 index units. The FRP comparison is much weaker: 35 positive matched windows, R² 0.101, RMSE 45.48 MW and efficiency −5.06. We retain this unfavorable result because it limits the method's use. Agreement between sensors does not supply independent ground truth, and positive-pair selection leaves observations unpaired.

The recorded reference identifies February, March and January as periods for closer review. February 2024 has 34.96 HHE against a recorded same-month median of 45.19. Its reference contains 20 recorded samples and zero established complete samples. The conclusion remains UNVERIFIABLE for a verified hazard claim because the detection archive does not establish complete observation coverage.

What makes the prototype useful

Five views connect the calendar, sensor comparison, manager brief and audit, schema mappings, and reproducible demonstration scenarios. Users can inspect an assumption change without replacing the original source. Downloadable CSV, GeoJSON, modeled schedule, receipt and audit ZIP retain the exact snapshot. The included offline verifier checks internal consistency; it does not authenticate the observations or certify scientific truth.

We built the application with Python, FastAPI and browser-native HTML, CSS, JavaScript and SVG. Analysis runs locally without a remote AI model or live network dependency. Keyboard calendar navigation, alternative data tables, reduced-motion support and responsive layouts make the evidence easier to explore. The current revision passes 179 automated tests; those checks demonstrate software behavior, not field accuracy or measured user impact.

Intended impact and next steps

Our intended benefit is a more careful, reproducible seasonal review before managers make decisions with local evidence. We have not measured operational benefits or completed land-manager interviews. Next, we will compare against independent incident and observation-coverage products, investigate FRP mismatch, and test the review task with land managers. Approximate satellite schedules remain illustrative; FireTrace does not provide operational alerts, burned-area estimates or verified fire causes.

Assistance and credits

We used Google Antigravity and OpenAI Codex for code debugging, review, tests, troubleshooting, and presentation drafting. Assistance also supported scripts for clearly labeled synthetic demonstration fixtures. The actual NASA case measurements were not generated or filled by AI. Screenshots show the implemented interface running locally; the submission includes no AI-generated photographs, video or audio. The application makes no live LLM calls.
